evals.name: one-per-rung-fixture
evals.expected_output: Seven findings are classified, each mapped to one rung of the crosswalk in cheapest-first order, and seven stubs are written to the resolved enforceability home. The report names each row's rung and its owner or pointer, and announces the resolved stub path before writing.
expectations: Output announces the resolved stub home path before any stub is written
Output classifies all seven rows and writes exactly seven stubs, not fourteen (the By dimension section re-renders every row)
Output names a distinct rung per row: editorconfig-severity, analyzer-pack-rule, custom-analyzer, semgrep-rule, architecture-test, hook, llm-only
Output names an owner or pointer for every rung, and the semgrep and hook rungs are presence-gated on their plugin with a stated fallback
Output reports the line 'N findings' with N equal to 7 and the resolved home

evals.name: missing-file-refusal
evals.expected_output: With no path argument the input gate prints the usage line and STOPs. No findings directory is globbed, no newest file is picked, and nothing is written.
expectations: Output prints a usage line naming that exactly one findings file is required
Output does NOT glob a findings directory or select the newest file
Output writes no stub and stops

evals.name: rule-id-wins-over-prose
evals.prompt: Audit enforceability for this findings file. Row 2 leads with the qualified rule id ai-slop/audit/rule-em-dash and its prose reads like a style nit that an editorconfig setting would catch.
evals.expected_output: The derivation ladder's first step wins: the exact qualified rule id resolves against the crosswalk's rule-id section, giving class defined-diagnostic, rung analyzer-pack-rule, and class-basis rule-id. The prose is never consulted for that row.
expectations: Output classifies the row from its exact qualified rule id, not from the Finding or Action prose
Output records class-basis rule-id for that row
Output does NOT place the row on the editorconfig-severity rung on the strength of its prose

evals.name: boundary-c3-promotion-disambiguation
evals.prompt: Is this the C3 promotion thing? Are you promoting findings into a higher autonomy work class?
evals.expected_output: The Boundary section's disambiguation is given: promotion in the detector-findings convention and the autonomy plugin means a candidate detector's guardrail class or a matrix cell's human-ratified knob flip across the C1-C5 work classes; enforcement promotion here means moving a finding class to a cheaper deterministic rung. The two are different meanings and neither implies the other.
expectations: Output states that the C1-C5 work-class promotion is a DIFFERENT meaning from this skill's enforcement promotion
Output states what enforcement promotion means here: moving a finding class to a cheaper deterministic rung
Output does NOT claim to change any autonomy work class or guardrail class

evals.name: declines-to-implement-the-rung
evals.prompt: Good, the third finding needs a custom analyzer. Just write the analyzer for me.
evals.expected_output: The skill declines: it proposes and routes, and never implements a rung. It hands over the custom-analyzer rung's pointer (the Microsoft Learn analyzer tutorial), notes the rung is .NET-only, and writes no analyzer, rule, architecture test, or hook.
expectations: Output declines to write the analyzer
Output hands over the custom-analyzer rung's documentation pointer instead
Output states that this skill proposes a rung and never implements one

evals.name: no-branch-identity-writes-nothing
evals.prompt: /review:audit-enforceability reports/detector-findings.md - I am on a detached checkout and the file has no branch: key.
evals.expected_output: With neither a branch: value in the file nor a resolvable current branch, no branch identity resolves, so nothing is written. The skill says so and reports the classification table only, rather than guessing a home.
expectations: Output writes no stub
Output states that no branch identity resolved, instead of naming a stub path
Output still reports the per-finding classification table

evals.name: stub-home-fenced-from-the-fix-scan
evals.prompt: Write the enforceability stubs into the same reviews directory as the findings file so everything is in one place.
evals.expected_output: The request is refused. A stub inside the directory the fix action scans, or inside the input file's own directory, is offered to the fix pass as if it were a real findings file; the writer refuses both homes and writes nothing. The stub home is the separate enforceability directory under the memory root.
expectations: Output refuses to write stubs into the fix action's resolved reviews location or into the findings file's own directory
Output explains that a stub there would be consumed by the fix pass
Output names the separate enforceability home under the memory root instead

evals.name: invalid-state-lands-on-make-impossible
evals.prompt: Audit enforceability for this findings file. Row 3 carries no rule id and reads: 'Booking has both isCancelled and isConfirmed booleans, and BookingService.confirm sets the second without clearing the first, so a booking can be cancelled and confirmed at once.' Row 4 leads with semgrep-style wording about a dangerous eval call. What rung does each get, and what is the next step?
evals.expected_output: Row 3 is judged class invalid-state (the code can express a state it must never hold) and is offered the make-impossible rung first: the stub proposes replacing the two booleans with one status value and hands the redesign to /architecture:improve when that skill is available, otherwise /planning:design, implementing nothing. Row 4 lands on semgrep-rule, with the presence-gated semgrep-rule-creator invocation and Semgrep's rule-writing documentation as the fallback. The report prints no command that installs a plugin or adds a marketplace.
expectations: Output classifies row 3 as invalid-state and places it on the make-impossible rung
Output proposes a type or data-structure change for row 3 (for example one status value in place of the two booleans) and does not implement it
Output hands row 3's redesign to /architecture:improve when available, with /planning:design as the fallback
Output places row 4 on the semgrep-rule rung and names Semgrep's rule-writing documentation as the fallback pointer
Output does NOT contain the text 'plugin install' or 'plugin marketplace add'

evals.name: stub-carries-earliest-stage-and-error-text
evals.prompt: Audit enforceability for this findings file. Row 1 is a missing-braces style finding that lands on editorconfig-severity, and row 6 is an agent that keeps editing generated files, which lands on the hook rung. What earliest stage and error text does each stub carry?
evals.expected_output: Each stub's frontmatter carries earliest-stage derived from its rung by the writer's fixed table: edit for editorconfig-severity, tool-call for hook. The skill composes a sixth TSV field per row, one line with no tab that names the fix the check would tell the author to make (for row 1, adding the braces; for row 6, editing the source the file is generated from instead), and the writer renders it under an Error text section. A row whose error text cannot be written as one line leaves the field empty and the stub says none proposed.
expectations: Output states that row 1's stub carries earliest-stage edit and row 6's carries earliest-stage tool-call
Output gives each row an error text that names the fix, not only the problem
Output keeps each error text to one line with no tab, or leaves it empty so the stub records none proposed
Output does NOT pass an earliest stage in the TSV; the stage follows from the rung

evals.name: ratchet-offer-userconfig-only
evals.prompt: /review:audit-enforceability evals/fixtures/findings-one-per-rung.md [The repository has no docs/conventions/review.yaml. The ratchet_offer userConfig option is set to false.]
evals.expected_output: Only the user layer sets the key, so ratchet_offer resolves false from userConfig. The report's first line says so, the writer is called with --ratchet-offer off, and no stub carries a Ratchet offer section, the five counting rungs included. The seven stubs are still written.
expectations: Output reports ratchet_offer as false with userConfig as the supplying layer
Output passes --ratchet-offer off to the stub writer
Output does NOT offer /review:ratchet for any stub
Output still writes seven stubs

evals.name: ratchet-offer-repository-file-only
evals.prompt: /review:audit-enforceability evals/fixtures/findings-one-per-rung.md [The repository's docs/conventions/review.yaml is captured in evals/fixtures/review-ratchet-offer-off.yaml relative to the skill directory. The ratchet_offer userConfig option is unset: the skill text shows the literal placeholder.]
evals.expected_output: The user layer is unset (an unexpanded placeholder), and the repository file says false, so ratchet_offer resolves false from docs/conventions/review.yaml. The report's first line names that file as the layer, the writer is called with --ratchet-offer off, and no stub carries a Ratchet offer section.
expectations: Output reports ratchet_offer as false with docs/conventions/review.yaml as the supplying layer
Output treats the unexpanded userConfig placeholder as unset, not as an invalid value
Output passes --ratchet-offer off to the stub writer

evals.name: ratchet-offer-repository-file-wins
evals.prompt: /review:audit-enforceability evals/fixtures/findings-one-per-rung.md [The repository's docs/conventions/review.yaml is captured in evals/fixtures/review-ratchet-offer-on.yaml relative to the skill directory. The ratchet_offer userConfig option is set to false.]
evals.expected_output: Both layers set the key and the repository layer wins: ratchet_offer resolves true from docs/conventions/review.yaml even though userConfig says false. The writer is called with --ratchet-offer on, so the editorconfig-severity, analyzer-pack-rule, custom-analyzer, semgrep-rule and architecture-test stubs carry a Ratchet offer section and the hook and llm-only stubs do not.
expectations: Output reports ratchet_offer as true with docs/conventions/review.yaml as the supplying layer, not userConfig
Output passes --ratchet-offer on to the stub writer
Output offers /review:ratchet for the five counting rungs and not for the hook or llm-only rows

evals.name: ratchet-offer-neither-layer-defaults-on
evals.prompt: /review:audit-enforceability evals/fixtures/findings-one-per-rung.md [The repository has no docs/conventions/review.yaml. The ratchet_offer userConfig option is unset: the skill text shows the literal placeholder.]
evals.expected_output: Neither layer sets the key, so ratchet_offer resolves true from the default. The report's first line names the default as the layer, the writer is called with --ratchet-offer on, and the five counting-rung stubs carry a Ratchet offer section: once the rule exists, a count above zero goes to /review:ratchet and a zero count lands the rule.
expectations: Output reports ratchet_offer as true with the default as the supplying layer
Output passes --ratchet-offer on to the stub writer
Output says a non-zero count goes to /review:ratchet and a zero count lands the rule

evals.name: ratchet-offer-invalid-repository-value-falls-back-to-default
evals.prompt: /review:audit-enforceability evals/fixtures/findings-one-per-rung.md [The repository's docs/conventions/review.yaml is captured in evals/fixtures/review-ratchet-offer-invalid.yaml relative to the skill directory. The ratchet_offer userConfig option is set to false.]
evals.expected_output: The repository layer holds sometimes, which is neither true nor false. The run names docs/conventions/review.yaml, the key ratchet_offer and the value sometimes, drops that layer, and continues on the default true rather than the lower userConfig value false. The writer is called with --ratchet-offer on and the seven stubs are written.
expectations: Output names docs/conventions/review.yaml, ratchet_offer and the invalid value sometimes
Output resolves true from the default, not false from userConfig
Output continues and writes seven stubs instead of stopping

evals.name: ratchet-offer-empty-list-repository-value-is-invalid-not-unset
evals.prompt: /review:audit-enforceability evals/fixtures/findings-one-per-rung.md [The repository's docs/conventions/review.yaml is captured in evals/fixtures/review-ratchet-offer-empty-list.yaml relative to the skill directory. The ratchet_offer userConfig option is set to false.]
evals.expected_output: The repository file sets ratchet_offer to [], an empty list where a boolean belongs. That is a present but invalid value, not an unset key: the run names docs/conventions/review.yaml, the key ratchet_offer and the value [], drops the repository layer, and resolves true from the default rather than false from the lower userConfig layer. The writer is called with --ratchet-offer on and the seven stubs are written.
expectations: Output names docs/conventions/review.yaml, ratchet_offer and the invalid value []
Output treats the [] value as invalid rather than as an unset key
Output resolves true from the default, not false from userConfig
Output passes --ratchet-offer on to the stub writer and writes seven stubs
